# Resolving payments stuck in UNKNOWN

> A scheduled job that finds payments stuck in UNKNOWN status, queries Stripe by idempotency key to learn their real outcome, and settles them through the ledger so orders react normally.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

When Stripe times out and Kafka retries run out of patience, a payment can get stuck in `UNKNOWN` status—we don't know if the charge actually went through. The `payments.resolve-unknown` job wakes up every 5 minutes and hunts for payments that have been stuck for at least 5 minutes. For each one, it asks Stripe "did you charge this idempotency key?" without ever creating a new charge. Stripe usually has an answer: if the intent succeeded, the job settles the payment as `COMPLETED` and records the money in the ledger just like a normal success. If Stripe says it was canceled or needs a payment method, the job settles as `FAILED`. If Stripe never saw it and 60 minutes have passed, the job gives up and settles as `FAILED` (it probably never reached the network). In all cases, settlement posts a journal through [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md) and publishes a payment response to Kafka so orders, notifications, and the shop balance read-model all react exactly as they would to a normal result. The whole settlement is one database transaction: the payment status updates, the ledger journal posts, and the outbox notification queues together. If a Kafka retry message already settled the payment while the job was thinking, the update will touch zero rows and the job backs off gracefully.

**Look at:** [`PaymentResolutionJobs` in payment-resolution.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payment-resolution.jobs.ts#L29)

## Pieces

- [Finding and dispatching stuck payments](resolve-method.md): Finds all payments in UNKNOWN status that have been stuck for at least 5 minutes (limit 100), queries Stripe by idempotency key for each, and routes them to settlement based on the intent status.
- [Settling the payment and recording the ledger](settle-method.md): Atomically updates the payment status and `providerRef`, records a marketplace sale journal if the status is COMPLETED, and publishes a payment response to Kafka through the outbox.
- Resolution and give-up timing constants: `RESOLVE_AFTER_MS` (5 minutes) is the minimum age of a payment before the job tries Stripe; `GIVE_UP_AFTER_MS` (60 minutes) is when the job assumes Stripe never received the charge and stops retrying.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | ``payments` table (Payment model)` | Reads payments in `UNKNOWN` status with `updatedAt` older than 5 minutes; writes status, `providerRef` to the row that matches the payment id and status. |
| external | `Stripe API` | Calls `StripeService.findPaymentIntentByIdempotencyKey()` to fetch the intent status by the payment's idempotency key; never creates a new charge. |
| database | ```ledger_entries`` table (via LedgerService)` | Writes a marketplace sale journal (with buyer, merchant, and platform fee accounts) when the payment settles as COMPLETED. |
| queue | ```payments.responses`` Kafka topic (via OutboxService)` | Publishes a payment response with idempotency key, `bisOrderId`, `userId`, amount, and status (COMPLETED or FAILED) so orders, notifications, and balance reads react. |
| job | ```payments.resolve-unknown`` cron job` | Registered on app bootstrap as `*/5 * * * *` (every 5 minutes); concurrency 1 and 120-second lease prevent overlapping runs. |

## Also relies on

- [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md): Reads and updates the Payment model with UNKNOWN status, idempotency key, and `idempotencyKey` to settle.
- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): Calls `LedgerService.recordMarketplaceSale()` to post the journal through the ledger when a payment settles as COMPLETED.
- [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md): Uses the same settlement path (ledger + outbox notification) as the normal charge success path, so orders and notifications react identically whether the charge succeeded immediately or was resolved from UNKNOWN.

## Watch out

- The job waits 5 minutes before asking Stripe—payments in UNKNOWN for less than 5 minutes are left alone so Kafka retries still have time.
- If a Kafka retry message settles the payment while the job is running, the database update will touch zero rows and the job silently backs off (no double-settlement).
- After 60 minutes with no Stripe record, the job assumes the charge never reached the network and gives up; this is permanent loss, not a retry.
- The job publishes the same outbox notification format as the normal charge path, so orders/balances/notifications don't know this was a retry—they react as if the charge succeeded initially.
